scope: This is the project’s named source set as of the date shown. It covers 72 video entries, including repeats, commentary and one unavailable playlist position. The audit screened 62 English or Italian caption tracks for technical terms, covering 106,452 cues. One additional recording has a separate publisher transcript. Eight other videos have metadata only. The 50 statements are attributed paraphrases with source clocks or document locations. Twelve written source records and seven pinned repositories were reviewed, alongside named articles, measurements, films and code archives. Book listings cover publisher information only. Source availability and scientific confirmation are separate questions.

items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He filled gaps experimentally for sub-aperture synthesis, registration and depth focusing. He describes his own implementation. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Fixed half-band reference (Human prompt following the band-pass filter design question)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He proposes a fixed half-band master and many partly overlapping half-band copies. English. Written prompt by Seyfzadeh; his technical interpretation, no Biondi confirmation.

items.title: Suggested 1-100 Hz range (Human question about whether seismic frequencies between 1 and 100 Hz are plausible)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He asks if 1-100 Hz could be the band for seismic frequencies. ChatGPT agrees. English. Written question by Seyfzadeh; model answer excluded.

items.title: Interpreting a surface ellipse (20:20 to 22:18)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He describes a surface ellipse from vertical and transverse oscillation as his interpretation, drawing on an external geophysicist. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Pairing two displaced looks (29:50 to 31:07)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He uses a single flyover, many Doppler sub-apertures, and slightly displaced reference and offset copies within each one. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Focusing against candidate depths (35:19 to 36:02)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He describes an adjoint focusing operator against theoretical phase histories for candidate depths. Biondi asks about the displacement matrix. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Encoding vibration direction (44:05 to 45:32)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He proposes extending the display to encode horizontal, vertical and oblique vibration orientation using a second polarimetry patent. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Choosing the section direction (55:24 to 56:28)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi recommends a range-oriented section. He describes lower quality when the line and sub-aperture split are both in azimuth. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Coarse and fine registration windows (56:37 to 57:11)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. His coarse registration frame is 128 by 128 pixels. The fine frame is 24 azimuth by 32 range pixels. He tested recovery with injected vectors. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Converting pixel shifts to metres (53:52 to 54:31)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He converts range and azimuth pixel scales independently to metres from delivered metadata. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Calibrating the rock-speed model (47:36 to 48:34)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He says he changed the rock-speed model, calibrated with Campbell’s Tomb and a shaft by Khufu, then applied the derived rule to Osiris. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Choosing the wavelength (1:21:43 to 1:21:59)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He says he used a different wavelength from 0.24 m and again cites calibration at Campbell’s Tomb. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Uncertainty in the depth estimate (1:21:22 to 1:21:37)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. Reviewing the Khafre similarity, Biondi says the depth estimate still needs work. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Changing the sub-aperture count (1:23:34 to 1:24:00)
items.description: Seyfzadeh, then Biondi. Seyfzadeh says K was 295. Biondi suggests trying 5000 after seeing the output. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Version and filter changes (1:26:56 to 1:27:39)
items.description: Trevor Grassi. He distinguishes a first Osiris output, a 100 m version described as 3360 pixels, and a later version with stronger filtering. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Aligning output with a drawing (1:28:02 to 1:29:00)
items.description: Trevor Grassi. He marked corresponding spots in Photoshop and discusses matching a perspective drawing to a different section view. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: First tests with a Capella image (37:30 to 38:00)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. Initial Giza tests used a lower-resolution image supplied without charge by Capella. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Sharing an image and a line (51:34 to 51:56)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He says a placement line was sent to Biondi and both had access to the image from Athanatos. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Confidence in the Osiris identification (43:48 to 44:04)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. His expressed confidence in seeing Osiris is above 50 percent and below 100 percent at this point. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Horizontal mismatch in the Khufu overlay (1:45:48 to 1:46:30)
items.description: Trevor Grassi. In his Khufu overlay, Grassi asks viewers to compare chamber heights and notes the horizontal mismatch. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Doppler bandwidth and half-band scanning (25:12 to 26:20)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes spotlight Doppler bandwidths of roughly 22-25 kHz and using half the available band to scan along the aperture. He separately mentions a roughly 10 GHz carrier. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Moving processing to GPUs (26:40 to 27:11)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi says they optimized the kernel and were moving towards GPU processing while retaining the same technique. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Retuning the method for depth (29:54 to 30:50)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says they tuned the software differently once the aim changed from the top of the pyramid to deeper targets. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Averaging several Gran Sasso sections (2:54:27 to 2:57:37)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. For the wide Gran Sasso target he describes wider focusing and averaging several lines pixel by pixel to reduce noise. He reports at least two months of processing. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Discarding noise-dominated outputs (20:50 to 21:30)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says they discarded many trials where noise was inverted and kept successes. He mentions hundreds of successes on other things. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: MATLAB to CUDA processing times (2:20:00 to 2:21:14)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes the Gran Sasso demonstration as software 1.0, a MATLAB to C++/CUDA rewrite, and a change from about a month to three or four hours. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Coherent processing of complex returns (23:35 to 24:45)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says the processing is coherent and handles real and imaginary components. It uses an aperture of displaced measurements to infer direction. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: A three-band colour image (33:05 to 33:38)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes a colour Capella image made from three Doppler bands. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Pseudo-inversion and the role of AI (55:18 to 57:10)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says the model is pseudo-inverted, reports four providers and distinguishes that reconstruction from AI. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Limits of spiral interpretation (47:17 to 50:09)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes the spiral as a shape. He cannot distinguish stairs from cables and describes material recognition as future work requiring ground truth. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Depth depends on the local geology (Podcast 23:30 (publisher segment timestamp))
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says accurate depth needs the local geological model and constant density produces only a rough estimate. English. Creator-supplied RSS transcript, paraphrased.

items.title: Unscaled depth axis in the spiral model (Podcast 26:15 (publisher segment timestamp))
items.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi says the displayed spiral model has an unscaled depth axis. He says in-person examination would distinguish what the apparent spiral represents. English. Creator-supplied RSS transcript, paraphrased.

items.title: Reading 648 m from a displayed ratio (3:02:15 to 3:03:43)
items.description: Khafre Project speaker at Bologna (Italian release). The presentation explicitly counts pixels relative to the 137 m height of Khafre and reads 648 m to the end platform. The speaker acknowledges obliquity and argues that the angular errors cancel in the ratio. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: A visible cutoff and deeper estimates (3:30:05 to 3:31:28)
items.description: Mixed panel; speaker changes in captions. The panel discusses a visible cutoff near 550-600 m and questions a deeper estimate. Attribution changes during the exchange. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Claim to have measured the Big Void (1:02:15 to 1:03:00)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says their model contains the Big Void and they measured its dimensions. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Separating Big Void and corridor priority (1:40:37 to 1:41:50)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. The conversation identifies Big Void on a slide. Biondi associates his six-month priority claim with the corridor in the following sentences. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Claimed orientation of the Big Void (5:19 to 6:00)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He tells Matt Beall that they detected the Big Void and offers a different orientation from the Grand Gallery. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Selecting the second-Sphinx search area (15:12 to 16:33)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes selecting the second Sphinx location after Damiano Piras and others suggested that area. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Compute requirements in meeting footage (11:40 to 13:50)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. In edited meeting footage, he describes using multiple cores and needing more computing capacity. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: An unspecified stage in the 2022 paper (50:05 to 51:39)
items.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. In his 2022 reading of the paper, he notes that he could not find a detailed explanation of one stage. This predates his later reconstruction. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Carlin Tunnel as a proposed example (Post text, Carlin Tunnel railway, Nevada)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes deep geocoding with one SLC and names the Carlin railway tunnel as an example. English. Author-written public post; paraphrased.

items.title: Program claims and intended external review (Initial report, abstract and project introduction)
items.description: Grassi and Frank Rogala. The program attributes deep imaging and material identification to the software and describes a proposed third-party check under NDA. English. Written program statement; paraphrased.

items.title: Eight shafts and two large chambers (Conference abstract, Second Step, March 16 2025)
items.description: Khafre Project (three signatories). The signed abstract describes eight shafts, two rows, 648 m depth and two cubes of approximately 80 m per side. It credits Capella and Umbra and multiple tomograms. English. Signed author abstract; paraphrased.

items.title: Tracking the Doppler centroid (1:12:18 to 1:13:09)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says changing surface motion shifts the estimated Doppler centroid. He records its history and attempts the inversion from it. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Vegetation as a source of noise (1:13:10 to 1:14:10)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi expects dense vegetation to add noise and says he has not tested strongly vegetated terrain. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Expected brightness of chamber edges (34:06 to 34:30)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says air inside a chamber should appear dark and its borders bright in his tomogram. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Extracting a section between two pixels (43:38 to 44:04)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He says to select two image pixels, draw a line and extract a vertical section. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Repeated Fourier transforms and runtime (40:01 to 41:04)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes calculating shifts with repeated FFTs and inverse FFTs over a large data region. He gives roughly two weeks of continuous processing for the example. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Proposed tests on the ground (48:50 to 49:54)
items.description: Filippo Biondi. He proposes ground radar and seismic/electrical methods to validate the satellite work. The phrasing is future tense. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

items.title: Malanga’s proposed independent review (22 September 2026 letter, Section 3, Fifth; Section 4)
items.description: Counsel speaking for Corrado Malanga. The letter describes the method as SAR Doppler tomography and multichromatic analysis of micro-motion. It announces plans for an independent review of the data and processing chain. English. Written statement on behalf of Malanga; paraphrased.

items.title: teoAmico/ResonarSat
items.description: Independent C processing chain. Examined the source and constants. No new full-scene Giza run.

items.title: mfwarren/Pyramid
items.description: Independent Sentinel-1 IW TOPS Giza experiments. Code and result JSON are public. Its explicit sensor and geometry choices differ from the Giza spotlight claims.

items.title: Hassanforeman/subsurface-sar-tomo
items.description: Independent controls-first tracker and depth-operator analysis. Executed the deterministic expected-power routine and checked its answer using independent QR and impulse propagation. Its null applies to accumulated and detrended noise.

items.title: not-JASH/sar-doppler-tomography
items.description: Independent CUDA chain and observation-space benchmark. Optional one-sided filtering encodes a sign convention. Blind recovery of physical polarity would need signed ground truth. The benchmark supplies its own forward-model observations.

items.title: simossss/sar-tomography-reproduction
items.description: Independent Umbra single-pass surrogate plus separate Sentinel-1 multi-pass test. The single-pass branch averages reconstructed complex values per subband. Its scores test a different observable from paired displacement.

items.title: emmanuel6474/biondirepro
items.description: Independent Vesuvius operator and published-figure audit. Useful control designs and source-fidelity checks. This is not Biondi’s processing source or a sensor-to-cavity validation.

items.title: juanvillaverde/harmonicsar
items.description: Public HarmonicSAR marketing site. The only JavaScript file in this revision runs the web interface and canvas illustration.
